drone: MikroKopter MK EASY Quadro V3, 4x MK3640/34 motors with a 16SoundsUSB card and an 8-mic MEMS cube hung 0.19 m below the motor plane
frame: Team XML frame: origin = centre of the cubic mic array; x, y = XML axes (normal to the cube side faces); z along the drone's vertical axis, assumed up; metres. Which horizontal axis points to the front (red) rigger is undocumented.

channel_map.source: KU_Leuven.yaml channel_map_source: assumption; only check = report's 1-based 'channel 7 is empty' matches the all-zero wav index 6

mic_pos.basis: XML values to 0.5 mm; NOTE possible mirror image of the physical array (open question)

rotor_pos.basis: KU_Leuven.yaml: radius 0.32-0.35 m by photogrammetry (+-3 cm); z = +0.19 m stated in the report

sources: report p.2 ('centre of the array lies 19cm vertically under the X-Y plane on which the motors lie'), Figs. 1-2
kul_cube8.notes: Channel index 6 is a dead mic (all zeros): use channels [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7]. Arms along the cube diagonals (+-45 deg from x/y); rotor set is C4-symmetric, so only R and the 45 deg placement matter until rotors are identified. Rotor rows are quadrant-ordered, NOT motor-identified. Takes include ~0.5-1 s spin-up / spin-down at the file edges.

open_questions: Array chirality: photos show each cube face's mic pair upper-left/lower-right, the XML predicts lower-left/upper-right -> the XML may be a mirror image of the build (KU_Leuven.yaml). GCC-PHAT on rotor noise peaks at lag 0 for every pair (coherent electrical/structural interference), so audio did not settle it.
Channel -> XML point map is assumed (Point k = channel k-1).
Rotor radius (~0.33 m) is photogrammetric; which motor sits in which quadrant is unknown.
